//: The home page's polyfill cards (polyfills: the MCP extensions; beyond: outside MCP) and audiences. Read by PolyfillCards.vue and scripts/agents.mjs; the audiences only by the latter (the Markdown copies for agents). Every line is taken from the repository's README and each polyfill's README, in the README's order: keep them in step when those change. The recordings are real Claude Code and Codex sessions, and each alt text says which.

polyfills.name: Events
polyfills.line: The agent watches events on your MCP servers, by poll, push or webhook, and an event wakes an idle session.
polyfills.alt: In Claude Code, asked to watch the acme-checkout Worker on Cloudflare and say what breaks, Claude starts a watch through Cloudflare's MCP server, run locally with a fix, delivered by webhook through a relay, and the session goes idle. When the Worker throws an error, the idle session wakes by itself with a prompt from the mcp-events plugin, reads the event and says what broke: a SyntaxError, where a request that expected JSON got plain text.
polyfills.addStep: Try it with the hosted demo server (no sign-in):
polyfills.ask: Give me a demo button and tell me what I type when I press it
polyfills.then:
- Codex: a woken session is a Codex CLI session (the terminal app or `codex exec`). A chat in the ChatGPT desktop app keeps its events but can't be woken, so ask it for `recent_events`.
- Pi: add the demo server with `pi mcp add feeds --url https://event-feeds.idosalomon.workers.dev/mcp`, then ask to watch for new earthquakes. Confirm the watch in Pi's dialog. An event wakes an idle session with a message starting `[mcp-events]` that says the extension sent it; Pi reads the event and answers.
- OpenCode: add the demo server with `"mcp": {"feeds": {"type": "remote", "url": "https://event-feeds.idosalomon.workers.dev/mcp"}}` in `opencode.json`. OpenCode asks before the watch starts, naming the server and the event type. Press the button: the idle session wakes with a message from the plugin, which the TUI shows as `◈ mcp-events: new events` and OpenCode Desktop doesn't show, and the model reads the event and answers.
- Muse Code: add the demo server with `muse mcp add feeds --url https://event-feeds.idosalomon.workers.dev/mcp`, then ask to watch for new earthquakes. The answer ends with a phrase such as `watch 4821`; type exactly that to start the watch. New events reach Muse with your next message: nothing wakes an idle session by default.

polyfills.name: Skills
polyfills.line: Skills an MCP server serves show up next to your own, load only after you say yes to each one, and are checked against the server's digests.
polyfills.alt: In Codex, in the ChatGPT desktop app, asked what skills the Hugging Face MCP server serves, Codex lists its 25 skills, all visible in Codex. Asked which GGUF quantization to use for a 7B model on a 16 GB Mac, Codex asks in its own form whether to load the skill huggingface-local-models from that server, saying its 4 files are each checked against the server's SHA-256 digest when read, with Do not load it, Show me its SKILL.md first, and Load it. After Load it, Codex answers from the skill: Q4_K_M.
polyfills.addStep: Try it with Hugging Face's public MCP server (no sign-in):
polyfills.add: claude mcp add --transport http huggingface https://huggingface.co/mcp
polyfills.ask: Which GGUF quantization should I use to run a 7B model on a 16 GB Mac?
polyfills.then:
- Claude Code: `/mcp-skills` lists what it serves.
- Codex: the served skills appear in the `$` list after you ask once to list the served skills, from the next turn.
- Pi: add the server with `pi mcp add huggingface --url https://huggingface.co/mcp`. Skills appear as `mcp-huggingface-<name>`, marked with their server. Loading one asks: "Don't load it", "Show me its SKILL.md first", or "Load it".
- OpenCode: add the server with `"mcp": {"huggingface": {"type": "remote", "url": "https://huggingface.co/mcp", "oauth": false}}` in `opencode.json`. Skills appear in OpenCode's own skill list as `mcp-skills:huggingface:<name>`, marked with their server. Loading one takes two steps: OpenCode's skill tool returns the plugin's note, then the model calls `mcp_skills_load_skill` and OpenCode asks: "Allow once", "Allow always" or "Reject".
- Muse Code: add the server with `muse mcp add huggingface --url https://huggingface.co/mcp`. Loading a skill waits until you type the phrase the answer gives, such as `load 4821`.

polyfills.name: Server Cards
polyfills.line: Name a company and the agent finds the MCP servers its domain publishes, and adds the one you pick. Servers behind OAuth work.
polyfills.alt: In Claude Code, What MCP servers does neon.com publish? lists Neon and Neon Docs from neon.com's own catalog, each with an Add button, and Add on Neon Docs marks it added, with a note to run /mcp to connect or sign in. Then the same in Codex, in the ChatGPT desktop app: Codex lists the two servers, and asked to add Neon Docs, shows its own form naming the host, the URL, the headers (none) and the Server Card it came from, with Don't add it and Add it. After Add it, neon-docs is in Codex's config; codex mcp remove neon-docs undoes it.
polyfills.ask: What MCP servers does neon.com publish?
polyfills.then:
Then add Neon Docs (no sign-in):

- Claude Code: press Add.
- Codex: choose "Add it" in its form.
- Pi: choose "Add it" in its dialog, which names the host, URL, headers, configuration file and undo command. Pi saves the server and connects it for the current session.
- OpenCode: ask "Add Neon Docs" and allow it when OpenCode asks. In the TUI the prompt says only "Call tool mcp_server_cards_add", with "Allow once" and "Reject"; the name and URL are on the model's call line above it. The server is in OpenCode's MCP servers at once, for this project, and OpenCode connects it.
- Muse Code: it writes nothing. Ask to add it, then run the `muse mcp add …` command it gives you, in a terminal or after `!` at the Muse prompt.

polyfills.name: Apps
polyfills.line: A server's app opens right under the tool call in the terminal, and answers the mouse and keyboard.
polyfills.alt: In Claude Code, Play DOOM opens the game from the hosted arcade server under the tool call, and it is played. A system monitor app draws a live CPU chart with a tooltip under the pointer, and in a terminal with no image support it draws the chart in text. Then a 3D torus knot renders inline and turns when dragged.
polyfills.addStep: Try it with the hosted arcade (classic shareware games from archive.org):
polyfills.ask: Find a shareware game in the arcade and load it

audiences.title: If you use an agent host
audiences.text: Install steps and a first run for each host. Pi extensions install from a repository clone; nothing for Pi is published to npm or Pi's package gallery. OpenCode installs each plugin from this repository on GitHub, with Git; nothing for OpenCode is published to npm. Muse Code installs the Codex plugins from this repository's marketplace.

audiences.title: If you build
audiences.text: The `create-polyfill` and `design-extension` skills, and the contract every polyfill here meets. New polyfills, and existing ones brought to another host, are welcome.

audiences.title: If you write specs
audiences.text: A polyfill can be the client half of the two implementations an extension needs to reach Stable.

beyond.name: ARD discovery
beyond.spec: Agentic Resource Discovery v0.91, a draft outside MCP
beyond.line: Finds MCP servers through a domain's ard.json, or by searching an ARD registry you choose, and hands the cards to Server Cards.
beyond.alt: In Claude Code, What does buildkite.com list via ARD? shows Buildkite's MCP server, listed by buildkite.com, with an Add button. Then a search of a local demo ARD registry for a server that checks CI builds: Claude Code first asks whether to send the query to that registry and up to three it refers to, and after Yes the result lists Buildkite and Netlify, each confirmed by its own domain, and says where the query went.
beyond.addStep: Not in the bundle. Install it on its own:
beyond.addCodex: codex plugin marketplace add idosal/AgentPolyfill && codex plugin add ard-discovery@agent-polyfill
beyond.ask: What MCP servers does buildkite.com list through ARD?
beyond.then: A domain lookup sends no query to a registry. A search sends the words of your request to the registry you chose, so every search asks you first and names where it's going. In OpenCode's TUI, the prompt says only "Call tool ard_search": the query and the registry you named are on the model's call line above it, and nothing on screen names a registry a referral names. In Muse Code, ARD finds servers by domain only, with no registry search, and gives you the `muse mcp add …` command to run yourself.
beyond.note: Installed separately from the others: a search sends your words to the registry you chose, so every search asks you first.
